(Herodotus 1:134.)
19480: Thou. Hebrew, Complutensian, and Sixtus V, "I may," etc. Septuagint, "and cast reproaches from thee."
19483: In the night. Or "early in the morning," de nocte, as the Hebrew implies. --- Curseth. His importunity will be equally displeasing. (Haydock) --- Flattery is dangerous, (Calmet) and unworthy of a free man. (Cicero, de Amic.)
19485: Hand. As it will flow away, such a woman is commonly incorrigible. (Calmet)
19486: Sharpeneth. Or instructeth. Fungar vice cotis. (Horace, Art.)
19487: Glorified. He who serves his master well shall be promoted.
19488: Are. Hebrew, "to men." Our hearts have all something similar. (Calmet) --- Septuagint, "as faces are not like each other, so neither are the hearts of men." They have all some peculiarity. (Haydock) --- But this agrees not with the original.
19489: Destruction. Hebrew abaddo, or abadon, Proverbs 15:11., and Apocalypse 9:11. People die, and are plunged in hell daily. --- Eyes. Avarice and ambition, Ecclesiasticus 14:9.
19490: Praiseth. If he be not puffed up, or if all agree in his praises, we may conclude that they are well founded. --- The, etc., is not in Hebrew, Comp.[Complutensian?], St. Jerome, or Chaldean, and destroys the connection.
19491: Mortar. Such were used by those who could not afford handmills. (Calmet)
19492: Flocks. John 10:3., and Ecclesiasticus 7:24. This may be applied to pastors.
19493: Generation. Thou wilt be cited as an example of prudence, if thou hast forseen the change of thy affairs, and provided for it. In the east it was not unusual to see a general of an army reduced to the meanest condition, and economy is necessary for all.
19495: Field. If thou wishest to purchase, or to pay the workmen.
19496: Milk. We cannot but admire such frugality. Septuagint are rather different; (Calmet) ver. 25., "Be careful of the grass in thy field....that thou mayst have lambs for thy clothing. 19498: Princes. Who each contend for the sovereign power. (Calmet)
19504: Poor. It seldom happens that the unjust leave their riches to their children, Proverbs 13:22., and Job 27:16.
19505: His. Septuagint, "he rendereth his prayer abominable."
19509: Mercy. This is true repentance, which enjoins, "not only to bewail past sins, but also to amend." (St. Ambrose, 2:Pen. v.) --- Sacramental confession was not required of the Jews, but they confessed their sins, when they laid their hands on the victim, etc., Leviticus 4., and 5. (Calmet)
19512: Prudence. Septuagint, "riches." Poverty is a great temptation to people in authority, more than avarice itself. (Calmet)
19516: Innocent. Unpunished, if he employ fraud, ver. 22., and Proverbs 13:21.
19517: Forsaketh. Hebrew, "oppresseth (Septuagint, selleth) a man." (Calmet) --- Neither small nor great bribes must be taken. (Justinian)
19518: Poverty. Septuagint, "the merciful shall have power over him," ver. 8. (Haydock)
19524: Men. Septuagint, "the just groan," and all are under "apprehensions." (Calmet)
19532: Corrupt. Hebrew, "scoffers," who provoke both God and men.
19533: Rest; or bring him to hear reason. (Calmet) --- Septuagint, "a wise man shall rule nations; but the wicked being angry, is laughed at, and does not frighten."
19534: Soul. They wish to protect the upright, Psalm 141:5.
19537: Enlightener. Septuagint, "visitor," with punishment, as they seem to speak of palliated usury, which cannot escape God. See Proverbs 22:2.
19542: Prophecy, by the urim, or by the mouth of prophets, who were in great power and estimation, 3 Kings 1:24., and 12:23., and 2 Paralipomenon 25:6., and 28:8. 19544: Amendment. St. Jerome (ad Evag.) says, after Thucydides: "Ignorance produces confidence, and learning fear."
19548: Soul, and exposeth himself to death, though this was only inflicted for stealing a man, Exodus 21:16. The night-thief might also be killed in the fact, Exodus 22:2. But if the person who had stolen denied it on oath, he was put to death for perjury, Leviticus 5:1.
19549: Fall. Human respects will not long preserve him from sin. (Calmet) --- Septuagint have a double version: "Those who fear and are ashamed of men, shall be thrown down.
